name: ValentinesPhotoShowcase
description: A project utilizing HTML,CSS,JS to make a website for your significant other showing off your pictures together.

paragraphs: A short page about the gap after a generated screen: auth that holds, an API the UI has to call, and the failure that shows up in the field. The live site is anthony-zhou.com.

The bench in section 02 runs locally. It does not call a model. A prompt earns points for a named audience, an output contract, concrete constraints, failure cases, acceptance checks, and non-goals. Adjectives such as “modern”, “scalable”, and “production ready” do not count unless the same line names a mechanism.
The rubric is deterministic and gameable. That is the point of having it in version control: a prompt change shows up as a score change, and the tests fail if the presets drift.
features: Demo — a generator can invent the rest. Easy to swap the author out.
Spec — the output is constrained, and a person still has to re-read every answer.
System — contract, failures, and acceptance checks are present, and the prompt names mechanisms outside the model.
